The standard initial diagnostic test for GCA is the measurement of inflammatory markers, such as C Reactive Protein (CRP) and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR), as they are typically elevated in this condition. The reasoning chain supporting the use of CRP aligns with medical consensus, as it is a quick and non-invasive test that can support the diagnosis of GCA. Angio Magnetic Resonance and Carotid ultrasound are not first-line tests for GCA but may be used in specific circumstances to assess vascular involvement.
